name: Zviti (Bou Saada Tomato, Garlic and Bread Mash)
description: The classic of Bou Saada: torn flatbread folded into a hot, crushed mix of tomato, garlic and chilli with olive oil and coriander, traditionally pounded in a wooden mortar and eaten with a cold glass of leben.

ingredients.name: kesra
ingredients.note: or any thick flatbread, about 100 g each

steps.text: Pound the garlic, chilli and salt to a paste in a large mortar (or pulse briefly in a food processor). Add the tomatoes and crush them coarsely; the mix should stay chunky.
Scrape into a wide pan, add the ras el hanout, black pepper and 2 tablespoons of the oil, and warm over medium heat for 8 minutes, stirring, until it is hot and just starting to thicken.
Break the kesra into walnut-sized pieces and fold them into the hot tomato mix so they soak up the juices. Take off the heat.
Stir in the coriander and olives, drizzle with the remaining oil and serve straight from the pan, with cold buttermilk to drink.

tips: Zviti is eaten hot and fast: the bread should be soft on the outside and still slightly chewy inside.
Use ripe summer tomatoes; with pale winter ones add 1 tbsp of tomato paste.

name: Mtabga (Saharan Stuffed Flatbread)
description: A two-layer flatbread of El Oued and Biskra, sealed around a soft filling of onions, carrots, peppers and tomatoes and cooked on a hot dry pan until blistered, then brushed with olive oil.

steps.text: Mix the semolina, flour, yeast and salt, add the water and oil and knead for 8 minutes into a soft, slightly sticky dough. Cover and rest 40 minutes.

For the filling, soften the onions in the oil for 6 minutes, add the carrots, peppers, chilli and garlic and cook 6 minutes more. Stir in the tomatoes, paprika, cumin and salt and cook, stirring, until almost dry, about 12 minutes. Cool.
Divide the dough into 8 balls and roll each very thin into a 22 cm round, dusting with semolina. Spread the filling over 4 rounds, leaving a 2 cm border.
Cover each with a second round, press and pinch the edges closed, and prick the top lightly with a fork.
Cook one at a time on a hot, dry heavy pan or griddle over medium heat for 4 to 5 minutes per side until blistered and golden.
Brush with olive oil, cut into wedges and serve hot, with a tomato salad or hmiss.

tips: The filling must be nearly dry, otherwise the thin dough tears.
Cooked mtabga reheats well in a dry pan.

name: Taguella with Lamb and Tomato Sauce (Tuareg Sand Bread)
description: The staple bread of the Tuareg of the Sahara, a thick unleavened disc baked under embers, broken into pieces and eaten with a hot lamb, tomato and chilli sauce. This kitchen version bakes it in a covered cast-iron pan.

steps.text: Brown the lamb in the oil in a heavy pot for 8 minutes. Add the onion, cumin, salt and pepper and cook 5 minutes.
Stir in the tomatoes, tomato paste and chilli, add the water, cover and simmer for 1 hour. Add the carrots and potatoes for the last 25 minutes.
Meanwhile, mix the flour, semolina and salt, add the water and knead hard for 10 minutes into a stiff, smooth dough. Rest 30 minutes.

Shape the dough into 2 thick discs about 2.5 cm high. Heat a heavy cast-iron pan or lidded casserole over low-medium heat and bake each disc covered for 12 minutes per side, until pale gold with a few brown spots. Bake without oil.
Brush off any loose flour, break the bread into pieces and serve with the hot lamb and vegetable sauce poured over or alongside.

tips: Traditionally the dough is buried in hot sand or ash; the covered pan imitates that gentle all-around heat.
Taguella keeps well; leftovers are good dipped in soup.

name: Tikourbabine (Kabyle Semolina Balls in Red Sauce)
description: A dish of Petite Kabylie: balls of coarse semolina dough steamed in a spicy red sauce of chicken, tomato, coriander and mint, cut open on the plate and soaked with the sauce.

steps.text: Mix the semolina with the salt and oil, then sprinkle in the warm water, working it with your fingers and the heel of your hand for 10 minutes into a firm, smooth dough. Cover and rest 20 minutes.
Meanwhile soften the onions in the oil for 8 minutes, add the garlic, tomato paste, paprika, harissa and pepper and cook 3 minutes. Add the chicken, salt and water, cover and simmer 25 minutes.
Shape the dough into 12 balls the size of a small mandarin, smoothing each with wet hands.
Stir half the coriander and mint into the sauce. Lower the balls in gently, spacing them out, cover and simmer on low heat for 30 minutes, turning them once with a spoon.
Lift the balls onto a large dish, cut each into pieces, ladle over the chicken and plenty of sauce and finish with the remaining herbs.

tips: Keep the sauce at a low simmer so the balls cook through without splitting.
Traditional versions use dried salted meat (gueddid) instead of chicken.

name: Kabyle Parsley and Potato Soup
description: A light green soup from the Kabyle kitchen: potatoes simmered in salted water, then parsley and lettuce leaves added at the end so they stay bright, blended smooth and served with chopped parsley and, if you like, a hard-boiled egg.

ingredients.name: fresh parsley
ingredients.note: plus a few sprigs to serve

steps.text: Bring the water to a boil with the coarse salt, bay leaf and thyme. Add the potatoes and cook for 20 minutes until very soft.
Chop the lettuce and parsley roughly (keep a few sprigs). Add them to the pot for the last 10 minutes of cooking.
Remove the bay leaf and thyme stalks and blend until smooth. Season with pepper and more salt if needed.
Serve hot, topped with chopped parsley, a drizzle of olive oil and quartered egg if you like.

tips: Adding the greens late keeps the colour and flavour fresh.
Rub toasted bread with garlic to dunk in it.

name: Kabyle Broad Bean, Courgette and Cabbage Soup
description: A hearty green-bean soup from the Kabyle kitchen: onions sweated in olive oil, then broad beans, courgettes and shredded cabbage simmered with coriander and cumin and served with garlic-rubbed croutons.

ingredients.name: fava beans
ingredients.note: fresh, in the pod, shelled about 400 g (or 400 g frozen)

steps.text: Sweat the onions in the oil over low heat for 10 minutes until they begin to turn blond.
Cover with the boiling water, add the salt, pepper, cumin and coriander, then the shelled beans, the courgettes and the cabbage. Simmer for 30 minutes until the beans are tender.
Meanwhile toast the bread cubes in a dry pan or oven until crisp and rub them with a cut garlic clove.
Serve the soup hot with the croutons. Mash a few beans against the pot side if you want it thicker.

tips: Skin the beans if they are large and mature, or the soup tastes bitter.
Fresh-picked beans need no soaking; use frozen when out of season.

source.title: Wikibooks (French) Livre de cuisine: Cuisine algerienne - Soupe aux feves

source.adaptation: Adapted from the 'Soupe aux feves' recipe in the French Wikibooks page 'Cuisine algerienne' (6 servings: 1 kg fresh broad beans, 3 onions, 3 courgettes, 4 garlic cloves, 1 small cabbage, bread croutons, coriander, 2 tbsp Kabylie olive oil, salt, pepper, cumin; about 30 minutes' simmering). Text rewritten; the water quantity, the shelled-weight note and the herb amount are the author's own. Page is marked as a work in progress.

name: Kabyle Mountain Couscous with Beef and White Sauce
description: A highland couscous with a pale, unconcentrated broth: beef shin cooked with onion and a little tomato, then carrots, turnips, celery, green beans, courgettes and chickpeas, served over twice-steamed semolina with no ras el hanout.

steps.text: Put the chopped onion, 1 tablespoon oil, the beef, tomato and water in the bottom of a couscoussier or a large pot. Bring to a boil, skim and add the pepper, paprika, coriander and salt. Cover and simmer 1 hour.
Rub the couscous with 2 tablespoons oil and the salted warm water until each grain is separate. Rest 10 minutes.
Steam the couscous over the pot (or in a steamer) for 20 minutes, tip it into a bowl, sprinkle with a little cold water and fluff with the remaining oil.
Add the carrots, turnips, celery, quartered onions and green beans to the pot and cook 20 minutes, then the courgettes and chickpeas for 15 minutes more.
Steam the couscous a second time for 15 minutes, until light and hot.
Heap the couscous on a platter, make a well, arrange the meat and vegetables on top and serve the broth separately.

tips: Taste the broth at the end: it should be gently seasoned, not red.
Without a couscoussier, steam in a metal sieve lined with muslin set over the pot.

source.title: Wikibooks (French) Livre de cuisine: Cuisine algerienne - Couscous montagnard blanc au boeuf
source.author: Wikibooks contributors

name: Chbah Essafra (Constantine Sweet Lamb with Almond Fritters)
description: A celebration dish of Constantine: tender lamb in a golden, gently sweet sauce of onion, butter, cinnamon, saffron and orange blossom water, served with fried almond-paste fritters.

steps.text: Put the lamb, grated onion, butter, cinnamon, turmeric, pepper and salt in a pot with the water. Bring to a boil, skim, cover and simmer over low heat for 1 hour 15 minutes until the lamb is tender.
Add the saffron with its water, the sugar and 1 1/2 tablespoons orange blossom water. Simmer uncovered 15 minutes so the sauce reduces to a golden, syrupy consistency.
For the fritters, mix the almonds, icing sugar, orange blossom water and just enough beaten egg to make a firm paste. Shape into 18 small balls and flatten slightly.
Heat the oil to 170 C and fry the fritters in batches for 1 minute until golden. Drain well.
Slide the fritters into the sauce for the last 5 minutes or serve them on the side. Serve the lamb with its sauce.

tips: Taste the sauce before adding the last sugar: it should be gently sweet, not sugary.
Smen (aged butter) gives the traditional flavour; plain butter is the everyday stand-in.

name: Bourek Annabi (Annaba Potato, Beef and Egg Parcel)
description: The big square bourek of Annaba: a sheet of brik pastry filled with mashed potato, spiced minced beef, cheese and parsley, with a raw egg cracked on top, folded shut and fried until crisp with the yolk just set.

ingredients.name: brik pastry sheets
ingredients.note: large, about 25 cm square (malsouka or warqa)

steps.text: Fry the onion in the olive oil for 5 minutes, add the beef, paprika, pepper and half the salt and cook 8 minutes until dry and crumbly. Cool.
Mix the mashed potato with the beef, cheese, parsley and the remaining salt.
Lay a sheet of pastry on the board and press a quarter of the filling into a flat nest in the centre, leaving a 7 cm border. Make a small well in the middle.
Crack an egg into the well, season it with a pinch of salt, then quickly fold the four sides of the pastry over the filling to form a sealed square, flipping it over if needed.
Heat the frying oil to 180 C. Slide each bourek in, seam side down, and fry 2 to 3 minutes per side until deep golden, spooning hot oil over the top. Drain on paper.
Serve at once, cut open so the yolk runs, with harissa and lemon.

tips: Work quickly once the egg is in so the pastry does not soak through.
Bake instead at 200 C for 20 minutes, brushed with oil, for a lighter version.

name: Djari Bel Foul (Constantine Broad Bean and Tomato Soup)
description: A thin red soup of the Constantine and Aures kitchens: lamb, tomato and skinned broad beans, thickened with fine bulgur and finished with dried mint and lemon.

ingredients.name: dried fava beans
ingredients.note: skinned, soaked overnight (or 300 g frozen shelled)

steps.text: Brown the lamb in the oil in a large pot for 6 minutes. Add the onion, paprika, pepper and cumin and cook 4 minutes.
Stir in the tomato paste and grated tomatoes, cook 3 minutes, then add the drained beans, salt and water. Bring to a boil, skim, cover and simmer 50 minutes.
Sprinkle in the bulgur, stirring, and cook 15 minutes until the soup is lightly thickened.
Stir in the dried mint and coriander and serve hot with lemon wedges.

tips: Skinned dried broad beans need about 1 hour of simmering; frozen ones only 15 minutes.
Use a spoonful of couscous instead of bulgur if you prefer.

name: Tiftitine (Ghardaia Handmade Pasta with Lamb and Date Sauce)
description: A pasta dish of the M'zab valley: small hand-cut semolina pasta in a red sauce where lamb is slowly simmered with tomato and a sweet infusion of dates.

steps.text: Simmer the dates in 300 ml of the sauce water for 15 minutes, mash and strain through a sieve to make a date juice. Set aside.

Brown the lamb in the oil for 8 minutes, add the onions and spices and cook 5 minutes. Stir in the tomato paste and tomatoes, then the remaining water and the salt. Cover and simmer 1 hour 15 minutes.

Make the pasta: mix semolina, flour and salt, add the water gradually and knead 10 minutes to a firm dough. Rest 20 minutes, roll very thin on a floured board and cut into small 2 cm squares. Dry for 30 minutes on a cloth.
Add the date juice to the sauce and bring to a boil. Drop in the pasta, stir and cook uncovered for 8 to 10 minutes until tender, adding hot water if the sauce gets too thick.
Serve in deep plates, with the lamb on top.

tips: Shop-bought small pasta (fregola, large couscous or short vermicelli) can replace the handmade pasta.
The date juice makes the sauce slightly sweet; balance with extra pepper if you prefer it savoury.

name: Poulet aux Amandes (Chicken with Onions, Ginger, Saffron Eggs and Almonds)
description: A gentle festive chicken: jointed chicken stewed with plenty of onion, ginger and parsley until the sauce is silky, served under toasted almonds and eggs tinted with saffron.

ingredients.name: fresh parsley
ingredients.note: chopped, plus a few leaves to serve

steps.text: Brown the chicken pieces lightly in the oil, then add the sliced onions, salt, white pepper, cumin, grated ginger and chopped parsley.
Cover with water, bring to a boil and simmer gently for about 1 hour, turning the chicken occasionally, until tender and the sauce is reduced and creamy.
Meanwhile hard-boil the eggs for 10 minutes, cool in cold water and peel. Steep the saffron in 100 ml hot water, add the eggs and simmer them gently for 5 minutes, turning, until golden.
Toast the chopped almonds in a dry pan over medium-low heat for 4 to 5 minutes, without letting them darken.
Serve the chicken on a warm dish with some of the reduced sauce, scatter over the almonds and garnish with the saffron eggs in quarters and parsley.

tips: Cook with just enough water to cover so the sauce reduces to a coating consistency.
Make the saffron eggs while the chicken simmers so everything is ready together.

name: Tajine Jben (Constantine Baked Cheese, Meat and Egg Tajine)
description: A golden baked tajine from Constantine: minced beef, parsley, grated cheese and eggs mixed into a custard-like bake that sets in the oven, sliced like a savoury cake and served with salad and bread.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180 C and butter a 24 cm round baking dish or tajine.
Fry the onion in the oil for 5 minutes, add the beef, salt and pepper and cook 8 minutes until it loses its raw colour. Cool slightly.
Beat the eggs with the cheese, parsley and nutmeg, then stir in the cooled beef.
Pour into the dish and bake 30 to 35 minutes until set, puffed and golden. Rest 5 minutes.
Cut into wedges and serve with a tomato and cucumber salad and bread.

tips: Use chicken instead of beef; boil it first and shred it.
Check that the cheese is made with non-animal rennet if you keep to halal.

name: Tbikha (Artichoke, Pea and Broad Bean Stew)
description: Algiers' spring vegetable stew: artichokes, peas and broad beans in a tomatoey, spicy sauce with garlic and cumin, served over rice.

ingredients.name: artichoke hearts
ingredients.note: frozen or jarred in water, halved

steps.text: Soften the onion in the oil for 6 minutes, add the garlic, tomato paste, paprika, cumin and harissa and cook 3 minutes.
Add the water and salt, bring to a boil, then add the broad beans and artichokes. Simmer 15 minutes.
Add the peas and simmer 10 minutes more until everything is tender and the sauce coats the spoon.
Finish with lemon juice and parsley. Serve over rice.

tips: Add 400 g of lamb in step 1 for a meat version, simmering 45 minutes before the vegetables.
Fresh artichokes: trim to the hearts and rub with lemon.

name: Sfiria (Algiers Buttered Crumbs with Chicken in White Sauce)
description: A dish of Algiers: dry bread crumbs warmed in butter until fluffy, topped with chicken in a pale cinnamon and chickpea sauce and sprinkled with cinnamon.

steps.text: Warm the oil in a pot, add the onion, chicken, cinnamon stick, chickpeas, salt and pepper and stir 5 minutes without browning. Add the water, bring to a boil, cover and simmer 55 minutes until the chicken and chickpeas are tender.
Lift the chicken out and keep warm. Reduce the sauce for 5 minutes if thin.
Warm the 3 tablespoons oil in a wide pan, add the breadcrumbs and 5 tablespoons of the hot broth, and stir over low heat for 5 minutes until fluffy and moist, but not soggy.
Pile the crumbs on a dish, arrange the chicken and chickpeas on top, ladle over some sauce and dust with cinnamon. Serve the rest of the sauce on the side with the eggs.

tips: Make crumbs by drying stale bread in a low oven and grating it; shop-bought plain crumbs are fine.
Use broth sparingly: the crumbs should stay light.

name: Badjidj Bel Batata (Salt Cod and Potatoes with Saffron and Paprika)
description: A fish dish of the Algerian coast: salt cod and potato slices simmered together in a paprika, saffron and garlic broth and finished with parsley and lemon.

ingredients.name: salt cod
ingredients.note: soaked 24 hours in several changes of cold water

steps.text: Drain the cod, remove skin and bones and break it into large chunks.
Warm the oil with the garlic over low heat for 1 minute, stir in the paprika, saffron and pepper, and add the potatoes and water. Cover and cook 15 minutes until the potatoes are nearly tender.
Lay the cod on top, cover and simmer 10 to 12 minutes, shaking the pot gently now and then instead of stirring so the fish stays in chunks.
Taste for salt (the cod is already salty). Sprinkle with parsley and serve with lemon and bread.

tips: Under-soaked cod will make the dish too salty: change the water at least 4 times.
Fresh cod works too: add 1 teaspoon salt.

name: Sdour Djedj (Algerian Chicken Gratin)
description: Soft chicken breast in onion and creamy white sauce, topped with melted cheese and baked until bubbling: the Algerian family gratin.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200 C. Fry the onion in the oil for 5 minutes, add the chicken, half the salt and the pepper and cook 8 minutes until opaque.
Make the white sauce: melt the butter, stir in the flour for 1 minute, then whisk in the warm milk gradually. Cook, whisking, 6 minutes until thick. Season with nutmeg and the remaining salt.
Mix the chicken and onion into the sauce with half the cheese and the parsley. Pour into a gratin dish.
Scatter the rest of the cheese over the top and bake 20 minutes until golden and bubbling.
Rest 5 minutes and serve with salad or rice.

tips: Add 200 g of sliced mushrooms or boiled potato slices for a bulkier gratin.
Choose cheese made with non-animal rennet if you keep to halal.

name: Yahni (Algerian Fried Chicken in White Sauce)
description: Chicken simmered in a light onion, cinnamon and chickpea sauce, coated in egg and flour, fried until golden and returned to the sauce with a squeeze of lemon.

steps.text: Put the chicken, onions, olive oil, cinnamon, chickpeas, salt, pepper and water in a pot. Bring to a boil, cover and simmer 30 minutes until the chicken is just tender.
Lift the chicken onto a plate, pat it dry and keep the sauce simmering to reduce by about a third.
Roll the chicken pieces in the flour, dip in beaten egg and fry in hot oil in batches for 3 to 4 minutes per side until golden. Drain.
Return the fried chicken to the sauce for 5 minutes, then stir in the lemon juice and parsley. Serve with the lemon wedges and bread.

tips: Do not let the sauce boil hard once the fried chicken is back in or the coating will slip.
The batter drinks sauce; keep extra hot sauce on the side.

name: Kamounia (Cumin Beef and Liver Stew)
description: A fragrant stew of beef and liver, built on a generous dose of cumin, garlic and olive oil and finished with parsley and lemon, eaten with bread or rice.

steps.text: Brown the beef in the oil in a heavy pot for 8 minutes, add the onion and garlic and cook 4 minutes.
Stir in the cumin, paprika, salt and pepper, add the water and bring to a boil. Cover and simmer 1 hour 15 minutes until the beef is tender and the sauce reduced.
Add the liver and simmer 8 to 10 minutes only, until just cooked through.
Sprinkle with parsley and serve with lemon, with bread or rice.

tips: Do not cook the liver longer than 10 minutes or it turns grainy.
Use lamb liver and lamb shoulder for a more traditional Maghrebi version.

name: Mdecha (Semolina and Mint Soup)
description: A fragrant, quick soup of coarse semolina simmered in a garlic, caraway and paprika broth and scented with dried pennyroyal mint, thick enough to eat as a light dinner.

ingredients.name: dried mint
ingredients.note: pennyroyal if you can find it

steps.text: Warm the oil in a pot over medium heat and fry the garlic for 1 minute without browning. Stir in the paprika, caraway and pepper for 30 seconds.
Pour in the water, add the salt and chilli and bring to a boil.
Rain in the semolina in a thin stream, whisking constantly to avoid lumps. Simmer over low heat for 15 minutes, stirring often, until lightly thickened.
Stir in the dried mint, taste for salt and serve hot with lemon.

tips: Add a handful of chickpeas or a diced tomato for more body.
Rub the dried mint between your palms as you add it to release its aroma.

name: Frites-Omelette (Algerian Fries and Egg Plate)
description: The Algerian everyday classic: golden fries folded into a spiced, well-set omelette, eaten from the pan with bread, tomato salad and harissa, or stuffed in a baguette.

steps.text: Rinse the cut potatoes, dry thoroughly and fry in the hot oil (170 C) in two batches for 8 to 10 minutes until golden. Drain and salt lightly.
Beat the eggs with the garlic, cumin, paprika, salt and pepper.
Pour off all but 1 tablespoon of oil from a wide non-stick pan, add the fries, pour over the eggs and cook over medium-low heat 4 minutes until the underside is set.
Flip with a plate (or finish under the grill) for 2 more minutes. Cut into wedges and serve with bread, tomato slices and harissa.

tips: Oven-bake the fries at 220 C with 3 tablespoons oil for a lighter version.
In a baguette with tomato and harissa it becomes the famous sandwich.

name: Doja Bel Bsal (Onion, Fennel and Mint Omelette)
description: A thick, soft omelette of slowly cooked onions with fennel and fresh mint, finished with a generous splash of olive oil. A traditional Algerian starter that works well as a light dinner.

ingredients.name: fennel
ingredients.note: small bulb, finely sliced, fronds saved

steps.text: Soften the onions and fennel in 2 tablespoons of the oil over low heat for 12 minutes until very soft and sweet, without colouring.
Beat the eggs with salt and pepper, and stir in the mint and chopped fennel fronds.
Pour the eggs over the onions, cover and cook over low heat for 8 to 10 minutes until the omelette is just set and the top is barely wet.
Slide onto a plate, drizzle with the remaining olive oil, cut into wedges and serve warm with bread.

tips: For a firmer cake flip it for 2 minutes.
Dried mint can replace fresh: use 1 teaspoon.

name: Dar Aami (Kefta 'Cigars' in White Sauce)
description: Little cigar-shaped kefta of beef, onion and parsley, simmered in a pale cinnamon and chickpea sauce and finished with lemon and egg yolk.

steps.text: Knead the beef with the grated onion, parsley, cumin, egg, 1 teaspoon salt and half the pepper. Shape into about 16 small cigars, about 7 cm long.
Soften the chopped onion in the oil for 5 minutes, add the cinnamon, chickpeas, water, remaining salt and pepper and bring to a simmer.
Lower the kefta cigars into the sauce, cover and simmer 25 minutes, turning once.
Whisk the yolk with the lemon juice and a ladle of hot sauce, stir it into the pot off the heat and serve right away.

tips: Do not boil after the yolk is added.
Brown the cigars in a pan first for a deeper flavour.
